frequency_question: How often do such intervention programs successfully reach their expanded scaling targets within their designated implementation windows rather than being capped, scaled back, or prematurely terminated?
membership_rule: Includes major U.S. monetary or fiscal intervention programs (e.g., QE programs, Reverse Repo operations, Treasury buyback programs, Supplementary Financing Program) where scale targets were set; excludes emergency single-day lending facilities.
provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named instances covering the entirety of modern quantitative and debt-management structural interventions by Treasury and Fed.
known_gaps: Excludes minor technical adjustments to small-scale standing facilities.
skeleton: 6 historical major operations/expansions reviewed; all 6 successfully achieved or exceeded their projected scaling and volume objectives once initiated by the principals.
validity_reason: Institutional operational mechanics for U.S. debt management and market interventions change slowly over decades.
